blocks.text: The parathyroid glands are four small glands on the back surface of the thyroid. They secrete parathormone when blood calcium falls. Parathormone makes osteoclasts (bone cells) dissolve calcium crystals of the bone matrix and release calcium into the blood, makes the kidneys reabsorb calcium from the urine, and activates vitamin D, which is needed to absorb calcium from food in the intestine.

blocks.caption: Imbalance of parathormone
rows: too much (for example from a tumour of the gland)
too much calcium leaves the bones, which soften and deform; blood calcium rises (hypercalcaemia), depressing the nervous system and weakening muscles
hypocalcaemia: neurons become more excitable; tetany, in which muscles stay contracted
